title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of safety glazing materials and their installation on vehicles (Safety glazing), version 1.12.0
scope_summary: UN R43 approves types of safety glazing material (windscreens, other panes and partitioning made of toughened, laminated, glass-plastics, plastic or multiple-glazed constructions) intended for vehicles of category L with bodywork, M, N, O and T. It also approves vehicle types of categories M, N and O with regard to the installation of these glazing materials, excluding lighting/light-signalling glazing, instrument panels, bullet-proof glazing, double windows and small plastic glazing not needed for the driver's forward or rearward vision.
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to: (a) Safety glazing materials intended for installation as windscreens or other panes, or as partitioning, on vehicles of category L with bodywork, M, N, O, and T; (b) Vehicles of category M, N and O with regard to the installation of these materials; In both cases to the exclusion of: (i) Glazing for lighting and light-signalling devices, instrument panels, special bullet-proof glazing and double windows; (ii) Small plastic glazing that is not required for either the driver's forward or rearward field of vision.
applies_to_components: Panes (side, rear, roof and other glazing other than the windscreen)
Safety-glass faced with plastics material (coated glazing)
Rigid plastic glazing and rigid plastic windscreens
Laminated rigid plastic panes and windscreens
Opaque obscuration and shade bands on glazing
Installation of safety glazing on vehicles of categories M, N and O
relation_to_other_regulations: Vehicle categories as defined in the Consolidated Resolution on the Construction of Vehicles (R.E.3), ECE/TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.7, paragraph 2.
Annex 22 refers to the procedure described in Addendum 6 of Mutual Resolution No. 1 (M.R.1) for determining the H point/R point and torso angle.
Annex 24 contains the vehicle installation requirements within R43 itself (no separate installation regulation).
Excludes glazing for lighting and light-signalling devices (covered by lamp regulations) and instrument panels.
Annex 5 notes uniformly-toughened glass panes may also be used as windscreens for slow-moving vehicles.

defined_terms.label: Toughened-glass
defined_terms.definition: Glazing consisting of a single layer of glass specially treated to increase its mechanical strength and to condition its fragmentation after shattering.

defined_terms.label: Laminated-glass
defined_terms.definition: Glazing consisting of two or more layers of glass held together by one or more interlayers of plastics material.

defined_terms.label: Ordinary laminated glass
defined_terms.definition: Laminated glass in which none of the glass layers has been treated.

defined_terms.label: Treated laminated glass
defined_terms.definition: Laminated glass in which at least one glass layer has been specially treated to increase mechanical strength and condition fragmentation.

defined_terms.label: Interlayer
defined_terms.definition: Any material designed to hold together the component layers of laminated-glass.

defined_terms.label: Safety-glass faced with plastics material
defined_terms.definition: Toughened or laminated glazing with a layer of plastics material on its inner face.

defined_terms.label: Glass-plastics
defined_terms.definition: Glazing comprising one layer of glass and one or more layers of plastic in which a plastic surface faces the inner side, other than safety-glass faced with plastics material.

defined_terms.label: Plastic glazing
defined_terms.definition: Glazing material containing as an essential ingredient one or more high-molecular-weight organic polymers, solid in its finished state and shapeable by flow during manufacture.

defined_terms.label: Rigid plastic glazing
defined_terms.definition: Plastic glazing that does not deflect vertically more than 50 mm in the flexibility test (Annex 3, para 12).

defined_terms.label: Flexible plastic glazing
defined_terms.definition: Plastic glazing that deflects vertically more than 50 mm in the flexibility test (Annex 3, para 12).

defined_terms.label: Laminated rigid plastic pane
defined_terms.definition: A plastic pane of two or more plastic layers held together by one or more plastic interlayers.

defined_terms.label: Laminated rigid plastic windscreen
defined_terms.definition: A plastic windscreen of two or more plastic layers held together by one or more plastic interlayers.

defined_terms.label: Double window
defined_terms.definition: An assembly of two panes separately installed within the same opening of the vehicle.

defined_terms.label: Multiple-glazed unit
defined_terms.definition: An assembly of at least two parallel panes permanently assembled in manufacture and separated by one or more gaps.

defined_terms.label: Symmetrical multiple-glazed unit
defined_terms.definition: A multiple-glazed unit in which all component panes are identical.

defined_terms.label: Asymmetrical multiple-glazed unit
defined_terms.definition: A multiple-glazed unit other than a symmetrical one.

defined_terms.label: Bullet resistant / bullet-proof glazing
defined_terms.definition: Glazing constructed so as to be resistant to firearms.

defined_terms.label: Principal characteristic
defined_terms.definition: A characteristic that appreciably modifies the optical and/or mechanical properties of the glazing, including trade names or marks.

defined_terms.label: Secondary characteristic
defined_terms.definition: A characteristic capable of modifying optical and/or mechanical properties, assessed via indices of difficulty.

defined_terms.label: Indices of difficulty
defined_terms.definition: A two-stage grading of variations in secondary characteristics where a change from index 1 to 2 requires additional tests.

defined_terms.label: Windscreen
defined_terms.definition: The glazing in front of the driver through which the driver views the road ahead.

defined_terms.label: Exterior forward-facing glazing
defined_terms.definition: Any glazing other than a windscreen installed in the front of the vehicle body forming part of the vehicle exterior.

defined_terms.label: Interior glazing
defined_terms.definition: Any glazing installed in a vehicle passenger compartment, e.g. partitions and separating windows.

defined_terms.label: Developed area of windscreen
defined_terms.definition: The minimum rectangular area of glass from which a windscreen can be manufactured.

defined_terms.label: Inclination angle of a windscreen
defined_terms.definition: The angle between a vertical line and a line through the top and bottom edges of the windscreen in the vehicle's longitudinal vertical plane.

defined_terms.label: Group of windscreens
defined_terms.definition: Windscreens of differing sizes and shapes examined together for mechanical properties, fragmentation and environmental resistance.

defined_terms.label: Flat windscreen
defined_terms.definition: A windscreen with no normal curvature giving a height of segment greater than 10 mm per linear metre.

defined_terms.label: Curved windscreen
defined_terms.definition: A windscreen with normal curvature giving a height of segment greater than 10 mm per linear metre.

defined_terms.label: Pane
defined_terms.definition: Any single piece of glazing other than a windscreen.

defined_terms.label: Curved pane
defined_terms.definition: A pane with a height of segment greater than 10 mm per linear metre.

defined_terms.label: Flat pane
defined_terms.definition: A pane with a height of segment equal to or less than 10 mm per linear metre.

defined_terms.label: Height of segment 'h'
defined_terms.definition: The maximum distance between the inner surface of the glazing and a plane through its ends.

defined_terms.label: Type of safety glazing material
defined_terms.definition: Glazing per paras 2.1-2.7 without essential differences in the principal and secondary characteristics defined in Annexes 4-12 and 14-19.

defined_terms.label: Nominal thickness
defined_terms.definition: The manufacturer's design thickness with tolerance ±(n x 0.2 mm), n being the number of glass layers.

defined_terms.label: Curvature 'r'
defined_terms.definition: The approximate smallest radius of arc of the windscreen in its most curved area.

defined_terms.label: HIC (Head Injury Criteria)
defined_terms.definition: A value characterising skull-brain injury from deceleration in a blunt perpendicular impact with the glazing.

defined_terms.label: Safety glazing material requisite for the driver's forward field of vision
defined_terms.definition: All glazing in front of the transverse plane through the driver's R point through which the driver can view the road when driving or manoeuvring.

defined_terms.label: Safety glazing material requisite for the driver's rearward field of vision
defined_terms.definition: All glazing behind the transverse plane through the driver's R point through which the driver can view the road when driving or manoeuvring.

defined_terms.label: Opaque obscuration
defined_terms.definition: Any glazing area preventing light transmission, including screen-printed areas, excluding shade bands.

defined_terms.label: Shade band
defined_terms.definition: Any glazing area with reduced light transmittance, excluding opaque obscuration.

defined_terms.label: Transparent area of the windscreen
defined_terms.definition: The glazing area within the design glass outline excluding allowed opaque obscuration but including any shade band.

defined_terms.label: Design glass outline
defined_terms.definition: The design maximum unobstructed vehicle aperture to be glazed, including trims but excluding obscuration bands.

defined_terms.label: Optical distortion
defined_terms.definition: An optical defect in a windscreen that changes the appearance of an object viewed through it.

defined_terms.label: Secondary image
defined_terms.definition: A spurious or ghost image in addition to the bright primary image, typically seen at night from bright sources.

defined_terms.label: Secondary image separation
defined_terms.definition: The angular distance between the primary and secondary images.

defined_terms.label: Regular light transmittance
defined_terms.definition: Light transmittance measured perpendicularly to the glazing.

defined_terms.label: Type of vehicle (installation of safety glazing)
defined_terms.definition: Vehicles of the same category not differing in manufacturer, type designation or essential aspects of construction and design.

defined_terms.label: Central driving position
defined_terms.definition: A driving position where the Y coordinate of the R point is at Y0 within ±60 mm.

defined_terms.label: Small glazing
defined_terms.definition: A pane with an area under 200 cm² within which a 150 mm diameter circle cannot be inscribed.

applicability_hints: Any glazing on L (with bodywork), M, N, O or T vehicles - side windows, rear windows, sunroofs/roof panels, partitions inside the passenger compartment - is a 'pane' or 'interior glazing' and needs R43 approval, not only windscreens.

Plastic (polycarbonate, acrylic) windows, including flexible plastic panes such as soft-top rear windows, fall under R43 (Annexes 14-19); only small plastic glazing not required for the driver's forward or rearward vision is excluded.
Glazing with coatings or applied plastic layers on the inner face (e.g. anti-lacerative/coated glass) is a separate class (Annex 9 / glass-plastics Annexes 10-11).
Multiple-glazed (double-glazed) units permanently assembled in manufacture are covered (Annex 12/16), whereas 'double windows' (two separately installed panes) are excluded.

Changes to interlayers, coatings, tint, obscuration printing or shade bands may change principal/secondary characteristics and require new or extended approval, and affect light transmittance requirements for driver-visibility glazing.
Glazing for lamps and light-signalling devices, instrument panel covers and bullet-proof glazing are excluded from R43.
Vehicle manufacturers of M, N and O need a separate vehicle installation approval (Annex 24) covering windscreen position, inclination and use of approved glazing.
Every glazing piece must carry the manufacturer trade mark and R43 approval marking, so replacement/aftermarket glazing also falls under R43.
